903: What to do in the moment
906: In situations of intense stress, anxiety or overload, the focus is not to solve the problem straight away, but to reduce activation and regain enough clarity to respond with greater control.
907: You do not have to apply every strategy. Often, a single technique practised for a few minutes is enough to reduce the intensity of the moment. If it does not work the first time, you can try another or repeat it.

980: Move for 2–5 minutes (walk, stretch, change position) to release physical tension.
981: If you prefer something more structured, you can try tensing and relaxing muscle groups (e.g. hands, arms, legs), focusing on the difference between tension and relaxation.

984: When you are stressed or anxious, you can use physical contact with yourself to help your body calm down. Try one of these options:
985: Place one hand on your chest and the other on your belly. Feel the movement of your breathing for a few cycles, without trying to change it.
986: Hold your own hands. Press lightly, as if you were comforting another person.
987: Cross your arms and hold your shoulders or arms. Apply gentle pressure and hold for a few seconds.
988: Press your feet against the floor. Focus on the feeling of contact and stability.
989: Stay in this position for about 30 seconds to 1 minute. On the next screen, the video shows the four options.
